validity.recommendation: Correct FuelSource 'Okaz Oil field' -> 'Akkas Gas Field'; the pipeline name 'Okaz' is a mistransliteration of 'Akkas' (Arabic عكاز) — rename to 'Akkas–Al-Anbar Gas Pipeline' and keep 'Okaz' as OtherEnglishNames. Endpoint province Al Anbar and destination (Anbar CCPP near Hit) are correct.
validity.researcher_notes: The row's ONLY cited source is the Al-Jibawi / Iraqi Economists Network PDF (June 2025), which the sheet transliterates as 'Okaz'. That PDF and every independent source actually name the source field 'Akkas gas field' (عكاز), a well-documented gas field in Al Anbar near the Syrian border — NOT an oil field, and not 'Okaz'. So the GEM FuelSource value 'Okaz Oil field' is wrong on two counts: (1) mistransliterated name, (2) it is a GAS field, not an oil field. The Al-Jibawi PDF (p. body + summary table row 4 'Akkas gas field - Anbar power station | 26 - 24 | Dry gas') describes SCOP planning a dry-gas line from the Akkas gas field to the Al-Anbar power station near Hit, in three sections: sec1 26in Akkas field->T1, sec2 26in T1->K3, sec3 24in K3->Anbar power station. P7460 (segment 'Okaz field-T1', 26in) = section 1. Independent corroboration: The National (2025-07-22) reports the Schlumberger deal to develop Akkas and that pipelines will connect the wells to central processing units feeding the Anbar combined-cycle power plant; Shafaq (2025-07-22) reports 'pipeline construction to connect Akkas to central processing units and power the al-Anbar Power Station'. Both confirm the field name Akkas and the pipeline-to-Anbar-CCPP function. Recommend correcting name + FuelSource. Existence and gas/transmission classification are NOT in doubt.

validity.recommendation: No merge — keep P7460/P7466/P7467 as three segment rows of one physical line, but flag them as a network in OtherEnglishNames/notes so they are not later mistaken for duplicates.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real — the Akkas gas field development and the dry-gas pipeline to the Anbar combined-cycle power plant are corroborated by multiple independent sources (The National 2025-07-22; Shafaq 2025-07-22; IINA 2026-01-15 drilling begun; power-technology.com Al-Anbar CCPP profile). Not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct — dry-gas transmission/feeder trunk from a gas field to a power station (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission both hold). DUPLICATE CHECK: P7460, P7466 and P7467 are the three SECTIONS of the SAME physical Akkas->Anbar CCPP line described by Al-Jibawi (Akkas field->T1 26in = P7460; T1->K3 26in = P7466; K3->Anbar power station 24in = P7467). This is legitimate segment granularity, NOT a double-count — do NOT merge, but they should be tied together as one network. SPEC: Diameter 26in for section 1 is supported by Al-Jibawi only (single strong source -> medium confidence for the number; no independent source gives per-section diameter). Length and Capacity are blank on the sheet and I could not source per-section values — the '250 km' figure reported for the SEPCOIII addendum is the WHOLE Akkas->Anbar CCPP pipeline, not this Akkas->T1 section, and the 100/400 MMSCFD figures are field production, not this segment's throughput — so I left them blank rather than fabricate.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'proposed' still holds. The project is clearly active (not stale): The National (2025-07-22) and Shafaq (2025-07-22) report the July 2025 Schlumberger field-development deal with pipelines to the wells/CPUs feeding the Anbar CCPP being contracted; IINA (2026-01-15) reports drilling operations have begun and phase-1 field production of 100 MMSCFD. NOTE / to re-check: Iraq Business News (2025-08-22, 'Iraq Authorises Pipeline Extension Contract with SEPCOIII') reports the Iraqi Cabinet authorised the Ministry of Electricity to sign a SEPCOIII addendum specifically 'covering the construction of the section from the Akkas gas field to the T1 station' of the ~250 km line — i.e. THIS exact segment moving toward construction. I could NOT cite that article as a status-change ref because iraq-businessnews.com returns HTTP 401 to url_verifier (bot-blocked), and no citeable source explicitly states this section is physically under construction (the citeable July-2025 wording is still forward-looking: 'additional contracts will be signed' / 'now under development'). To avoid an unsourced upgrade I keep 'proposed'; if Baird can access the SEPCOIII source or find another outlet naming the Akkas->T1 construction contract, this likely warrants a change to 'construction' with ConstructionYear=2025. Not stale under dormancy rules (evidence within 6 months).

summary: P7460 exists and is correctly classed (dry-gas transmission section 1, Akkas field->T1, of the Akkas->Anbar CCPP line), but name 'Okaz' and FuelSource 'Okaz Oil field' are wrong (it is the Akkas GAS field); P7466/P7467 are the other two sections (segments, not duplicates); status 'proposed' confirmed active (drilling begun Jan 2026).
